clauses.mechanism: one_time_revocation_performed_on_stated_effective_date (own terms: effective at the close of business December 31, 1944)
clauses.reason: whole: The designation of Dunkirk, New York, as a customs port of entry is revoked "effective at the close of business" December 31, 1944 (the date is split across two printed lines). The revocation is a one-time command performed at the close of business on 1944-12-31, so the order is exhausted by performance on that date (the exclusive reading is that it ends as that day closes, which is the same instant); the designation stays revoked as a surviving consequence. The order has no sunset, report or continuing duty.

research_rationale:
EO 9504 (signed November 27, 1944; F.R. Doc. 44-18118, filed November 28, 1944) was read in full in the registered held text (machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF, grade original_representation_unverified, under jobs/fr-originals); the heading, body, signature, date and filing line were read; page images were not compared. Under section 1 of the act of August 1, 1914 (19 U.S.C. 2) it revokes the designation of Dunkirk, New York, as a customs port of entry in Customs Collection District Number 9 (Buffalo), effective at the close of business December 31, 1944. The revocation is a one-time command performed on that date; the designation stays revoked as a surviving consequence. The later effective date is the order's own term. AI producer hypothesis only; not human certification.
